headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but non-zero due to shared file-based workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes project files and uses a review-then-apply workflow, while unstructured processes documents and text. If unstructured outputs are placed into the shared workspace, Plandex can ingest attacker-controlled content as trusted input. The pair has a file bridge, so injection is plausible even without a direct API bridge.
conditions: IF unstructured outputs are written into Plandex's project directory or plan-local sandbox
IF Plandex parses document text as instructions during review or apply
mitigations: Keep unstructured outputs in a separate directory
Require a human review step before Plandex consumes extracted text
Prefix extracted text with a non-executable marker header
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between extraction and planning

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystem content, and Plandex explicitly handles model-provider API keys while unstructured processes documents and images. In a shared workspace, document contents can flow into Plandex's inference context or logs, creating a realistic leakage path. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary between them.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted volume
IF sensitive documents are passed from unstructured into Plandex for planning or summarization
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Do not place secrets in files processed by unstructured
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Restrict Plandex to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write and subprocess execution, and Plandex also has broad network egress plus git-state modification. In a shared directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and no locking mechanism is documented in either profile. This matches the high-risk overlap pattern more closely than medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or output directory
IF git state is modified by Plandex while unstructured writes derived artifacts into the same tree
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a manual lock file
Run unstructured in read-only mode on source inputs
Pause Plandex auto-apply during extraction runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner that can act on files, while unstructured produces extracted documents/text that Plandex may treat as authoritative input. If extracted content is wrong or adversarial, Plandex can propagate it into plans or code changes without a verification layer. The profiles show a plausible handoff but not an explicit downstream action agent, so medium fits.
conditions: IF unstructured output is fed directly into Plandex prompts or plan files
IF Plandex applies changes without a separate verification pass
mitigations: Require source-document citations in Plandex plans
Compare extracted text against originals before apply
Use a second human reviewer for high-impact changes
Disable auto-apply for document-derived tasks
requires-engineering: add validation checks between extraction and planning

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Plandex mentions model-provider API keys and cloud/self-hosted calls, while unstructured exposes privacy-policy and docs endpoints, but the profiles do not establish a concrete compliance conflict. The other agent is not cited because no mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through a third-party model provider via Plandex
IF the deployment uses a jurisdictional policy not shown in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Review vendor privacy terms before deployment
Keep processing self-hosted where possible
Log data classes sent to external APIs
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
